plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 9: Systems of Equations and Inequalities
plan.contextChunk: This figure places three small drawings in a row, each pairing a circle with a straight line rendered as a blue double-headed arrow, to enumerate how many points the two curves can share. In the leftmost drawing the circle is orange and the blue line passes above and to the left of it without ever touching the rim; the label beneath reads "No solutions." In the center drawing the circle is green and the blue line rises steeply from lower left to upper right, grazing the circle at a single point on its upper-left edge, which is marked with a filled black dot; the label beneath reads "One solution." In the rightmost drawing the circle is red and the blue line cuts through it, entering at the lower left and exiting at the upper right; the upper-right crossing is visibly marked with a filled black dot while the second crossing is implied by the line passing through the circle. The label beneath reads "Two solutions." The three panels hold the circle size and the line's slope fixed and change how far the line sits from the center, so the number of circle-line intersections is the variable. Together they lay out the complete range of outcomes for a system built from a circle and a line.

interactionPlan.concept: A system of a circle and a line can have zero, one, or two solutions, and which case occurs is determined entirely by the perpendicular distance from the circle's center to the line — equivalently by the sign of the discriminant of the resulting quadratic.
elements: Three side-by-side panels sharing a common baseline
Left panel: orange circle, fixed radius, centered in panel
Center panel: green circle, same radius
Right panel: red circle, same radius
Blue double-headed arrow line in each panel, all with identical positive slope (~60° from horizontal), arrowheads at both ends
Left panel line: passes above and to the left of the orange circle, no contact
Center panel line: tangent to the green circle at its upper-left edge
Right panel line: secant through the red circle, entering lower-left and exiting upper-right
Filled black dot marking the tangency point in the center panel
Filled black dots marking the two crossing points in the right panel (upper-right crossing emphasized)
Caption labels beneath each panel: 'No solutions', 'One solution', 'Two solutions' in serif type
Dashed perpendicular segment from circle center to the line (distance d) shown when active
Radius segment r drawn from center in the active panel for comparison with d
Equation panel (alternate view): circle equation x² + y² = r², line equation y = mx + b, substituted quadratic, discriminant expression and its sign
Solution-count readout badge (0, 1, or 2) tied to the active configuration

interactions.label: Line offset from center (distance d, in units of radius r)
interactions.teaches: Sliding the line parallel to itself makes intersection points appear, merge, and vanish — the count depends only on whether d is greater than, equal to, or less than the radius.

interactions.label: Step through cases
interactions.teaches: The three panels are not three unrelated pictures but the three exhaustive outcomes of one circle-line system.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The visual number of crossings is the same information as the sign of the discriminant of the quadratic obtained by substitution.

interactions.label: Show distance d and radius r
interactions.teaches: Comparing the perpendicular distance from center to line against the radius is the single test that decides the case.

demo_steps.title: Three possible outcomes
demo_steps.narration: Three circles, three parallel lines with the same slope. Only the line's distance from the center changes, and with it the number of shared points.

demo_steps.title: No solutions: the line misses
demo_steps.narration: The line passes entirely outside the orange circle. No point satisfies both equations, so the system has no solution.

demo_steps.title: One solution: tangency
demo_steps.narration: Slide the line inward until d equals exactly the radius. The two would-be crossings merge into a single tangency point, marked in black.

demo_steps.title: Two solutions: a secant
demo_steps.narration: Push the line closer still. It now cuts the circle, entering at the lower left and exiting at the upper right — two marked intersection points, two solutions.

demo_steps.title: The algebra behind the picture
demo_steps.narration: Substituting the line into the circle gives a quadratic. Its discriminant is negative, zero, or positive exactly when the line misses, touches, or cuts the circle.

demo_steps.title: Sweep and watch the discriminant
demo_steps.narration: Drag the offset slider across the full range and watch the discriminant change sign at the tangent case — the geometric and algebraic tests are the same test.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The number of solutions is decided by a single comparison: distance from center to line versus radius — d > r gives none, d = r gives one, d < r gives two, and this is precisely the sign of the discriminant.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Horizontal row of three equal-size panels on white. Circles are thin-stroked outlines in orange (left), green (center), red (right), all the same radius and vertically centered. Each panel carries one steel-blue double-headed arrow line at the same steep positive slope (~60°), drawn thin with arrowheads at both ends extending past the panel content. Left line clears the circle up and to the left; center line grazes the upper-left rim at one small filled black dot; right line slices through, with filled black dots at both crossings (upper-right one most prominent). Serif captions centered below each panel: 'No solutions', 'One solution', 'Two solutions'. When showDistance is on, draw a thin gray dashed perpendicular from the circle center to the line labeled d, plus a light gray radius segment labeled r, in the active panel. Active panel is emphasized (slightly enlarged, others dimmed) while stepping cases. In Algebraic view, replace the drawings with a clean centered equation card: x² + y² = r² above y = mx + b, then the substituted quadratic (1+m²)x² + 2mbx + (b² − r²) = 0, then D = 4m²b² − 4(1+m²)(b² − r²) with its numeric value color-coded red for D<0, black for D=0, green for D>0, and a large badge reading 0, 1, or 2 solutions.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for line offset from the circle center: the learner drags the line parallel to itself, the number of marked intersections changes from zero to one to two, and distance from center to line determines the solution count.
- Button for cases: the learner steps through no solution, tangent, and secant views, the active panel enlarges and marks only the current intersection points, making the three possible circle-line systems distinct.
- Toggle between geometric and equation view: the learner switches from the drawings to a small equation panel showing discriminant sign, and the visual count of intersections connects to the algebraic number of solutions.

The figure illustrates possible solution sets for a system of equations involving a circle and a line.

An illustration showing the three possible numbers of intersection points between a line and a circle: zero (no solutions), one (a tangent line), or two (a secant line).

discrepancies: Circle-to-panel scale is smaller than the source: source circles nearly fill each panel (diameter ≈ 70% of panel width) while the generated circles occupy roughly half, leaving more empty space and making the arrows look proportionally long.

In the source the red 'Two solutions' chord passes close to the circle centre with the two dots well separated near the upper-right and lower-left rim; the generated version places the chord noticeably off-centre so one dot sits at the top of the circle rather than on the upper-right arc.

The source line arrowheads are slender open-V style with relatively long shafts; the generated ones are filled solid triangles and the shafts are clipped to a tighter box, giving a slightly different visual weight.
The generated red circle (#C1252E) is a touch darker/more crimson than the source's brighter red, and the tangent dot on the green panel sits slightly higher on the arc than in the source.

Extra on-canvas content not in the source (dashed d segment, r segment, 'd = 1.60 r > r → 0 solutions' readout, full algebraic-view panel) appears once toggles/steps are used — acceptable as added pedagogy but it changes the composition away from the clean three-panel source.
evaluation.notes: A faithful and well-labelled three-panel reproduction (orange miss / green tangent / red secant with correct captions and serif styling) backed by genuinely meaningful interactions — offset slider, case stepper, distance overlay, algebraic view and a 6-step tour — with only modest scale and chord-placement deviations from the source.

feedback.rationale: No failure modes or action items remain and all scores are strong with verification clean; the listed discrepancies are minor cosmetic deviations not worth another iteration.
